raw_response:
I farm this kind of land the way I always have: I start from what worked last year, then I nudge it a little if prices, water, or labor push me. On 30 mu, I will still keep most of the land in wheat-maize because that is the steady part of the income and I have well water, so I can protect yield. I will not spread myself too thin on cash crops, but I will keep some cotton because it still gives me a chance at better cash if the stand is good, and I will keep a small piece of garlic because it brings money early and the area is small enough to manage. I finished primary school, so I do look at seed dealers and what people nearby do, but in the end I trust what I have seen on fields around me. For fertilizer, I will not gamble low. Wheat and maize feed the family and the farm cash flow, so I will keep nitrogen a bit full, with phosphorus under the base fertilizer and some potassium where I think the land is getting tired. Cotton needs feeding later, not all at once, and I will spray it more times because insects can ruin that crop fast. Garlic I will keep on the better piece of land, with more water and more compound fertilizer, because if garlic is weak from the start it never catches up. Since I have 30 mu, I think more about keeping the whole farm running smoothly than saving a tiny bit on each bag, so I will spend enough on fertilizer, water, and sprays to make sure the crop does not fall behind.
